Position Summary

Two Sigma is a leading quantitative investment management and trading firm. The company applies a scientific approach to investing, combining cutting-edge technology, artificial intelligence, data science, and quantitative research with rigorous human inquiry to capitalize on market opportunities and deliver alpha for investors.

Our team of engineers, quantitative researchers and data scientists looks beyond the traditional to test hypotheses and develop creative solutions to some of the world’s most complex economic problems.

We are seeking a talented Data Operations Analyst to join our Global Data Operations team in London. GDO is a service provider for data-driven operations and operational risk management: we create, maintain, and operate the optimized workflows that provide and curate the data used in live trading. You’ll be part of a close-knit, global team whose daily execution is essential to the success of Two Sigma’s business.

This is a hands-on, technical operating role. We are looking for someone who is comfortable at the level of the database, the shell, the job log, and the file system, who can pull apart a problem with a diverse set of tools, and who wants to make our operations measurably better by writing and improving the runbooks we run every day.

You Will Take On The Following Responsibilities

Investigate and remediate production alerts using incident-specific runbooks, owning each issue through to resolution or escalation
Author and improve runbooks, applying existing data-management workflow standards, turning recurring, ad-hoc fixes into clear, unambiguous, repeatable procedures that lower operational risk and increase throughput
Mine our data to surface patterns and help root-cause issues, validate data, and reveal trends across large volumes
Apply predefined acceptance and quality criteria to guarantee the integrity of financial data sets
Collaborate with business partners, software engineers, data analysts, and other data operations specialists to understand and improve business processes
Recommend and improve data-management policies and procedures to improve efficiency and accuracy

You Should Possess The Following Qualifications

Comfort with underlying technology. You can work behind the UI: the UNIX/Linux command line, querying databases (SQL) to mine and validate data, reading logs, and navigating file systems, schedulers, and storage
Exposure to scripting – Bash, Python, or a similar language – and the judgment to know when a script helps and when a runbook is the right answer
A genuine pull toward operations: you like to execute daily, at volume, follow workflows to the letter, and feel the immediate impact of work done right
Comfort switching between systems and tools – Linux/Windows, database/file-server, UI/command-line, text/numbers – without being dependent on a single framework
Strong attention to detail and exceptional verbal and written communication
BS in a technical discipline or equivalent hands-on experience in a comparable operational or technical role
Minimum 1 year of experience required; 1-5 years of experience preferred

Preferred Experience

Professional experience in data operations, technical operations, or a similar discipline – e.g. data operations analyst, systems/support engineer, data analyst, process engineer, systems administration, QA, or a structured operational background such as defense analysis, logistics, or maintenance technician work where you followed and built step-by-step procedures and worked with data and tooling
Hands-on experience performing data-management and data-quality tasks in data-intensive environments
A desire to grow your knowledge of finance and trading

Hours Notice

This is a London-hours operational role within a global team supporting trading 24/5 across Houston, Tokyo, and London. The work is interrupt-driven and time-sensitive, with early starts (from approximately 7:00 AM London time) to cover the period before and during the trading day. Out-of-hours and weekend support are not required.

GC AI is the fastest-growing and most trusted legal AI platform for in-house legal teams. We're building the future of legal work, and we're doing it fast. You'll join at a pivotal moment—when decisions matter, impact is immediate, and the runway to shape your career is wide open. We’re a high-performing team where you'll have real ownership and influence from day one.

More than 1,800 companies use GC AI to drive their business forward, including 150+ public companies, 25+ unicorns, and brands such as News Corp, Miro, Bass Pro Shops, Snyk, Skims, Liquid Death, Vercel, Zscaler, and TIME.

We've 10x'd revenue in 12 months, raised a $60 million Series B ($555 million valuation), and are growing faster than ever. We are backed by incredible investors, including Scale Venture Partners, Northzone, Sound Ventures, and Guillermo Rauch, CEO of Vercel.

If you thrive when the stakes are high and the path isn't paved, you'll love it here. Our six guiding principles are: 1% better every day, customer obsession, ship today, find a way, care deeply, and own it completely. Come shape the future of legal work with us.

About The Role

GC AI is hiring its first Technical Program Manager at an important time. Revenue has grown 10x in the past year; we are shipping quickly and taking on more projects than ever. We need a clear way to see what is happening across those projects, make hard choices early, and ship reliably.

This is a build-from-scratch role. You will create the system for moving work from an idea to something customers can use. Everyone should know what is on track, what is at risk, what is likely to ship, and where a decision is needed. Your job is to make delivery clearer and faster—not to add unnecessary process.

We have already started. Our Launch Calendar shows upcoming releases, owners, key dates, launch briefs, and whether each team is ready. Calvin, our launch intake agent, turns a Slack conversation into a launch entry. These are early pieces of a much bigger system. They also show how we like to work: build something useful, put it into the real workflow, and improve it over time.

You will report to engineering leadership and work with Engineering, Product, Marketing, Legal, Sales, and outside partners. This is not a role where you only update plans and report status. You will improve how the company works, run our most important launches, and build some of the tools and automations yourself.

What You'll Do

Learn how work moves from an idea to a customer. Find where it gets stuck, clarify ownership, and help teams close the gaps.
Keep a clear view of all major projects. Help teams set priorities, plan the order of work, and spot conflicts or dependencies early.
Set up and run a simple, useful project and launch reviews. Make sure decisions are made quickly, and automate follow-up when possible.
Lead our most important launches. Raise risks early and help teams make hard choices about scope, quality, timing, and what should happen first.
Improve the Launch Calendar and Calvin. Use agents and automations to collect updates, find risks, build launch briefs, send work for review, and notify the right people when plans change.
Pull information from Notion, Slack, Linear, and other tools into one clear view. Leaders should know what is on track, what is likely to ship, and what needs help.
Create simple playbooks, decision logs, and dependency lists so teams do not lose important context.
Make sure Marketing, Legal, Sales, customers, and outside partners get the information and time they need before a launch.
Get teams to use the systems you build. Measure whether they save time, remove blockers, and help us ship faster without adding busywork.

What You've Done

You have 7+ years of experience shipping complicated software across several teams.
You have built a new way of working, gotten people to use it, and made it better over time.
You build things yourself. You may write code, build agents, connect APIs, or make the first version of a tool.
You understand how AI products are built. You can talk with engineers about models, evaluations, data, APIs, speed, reliability, and the choices involved in shipping them.
Engineers trust you because you understand the details, ask good questions, and help teams make sound decisions.
You can explain a complicated technical problem to leaders in simple terms: what needs to be decided, what the options are, and what happens if we wait.
You use data and conversations to find the real problem, then help people solve it with calm and urgency.
You can build trust across teams, even when plans change, deadlines slip, or people disagree.
You like building from scratch. A blank page excites you.

NICE TO HAVE

You have been the first PM, TPM, chief of staff, engineering operations lead, or similar hire at an early-stage company.
You have worked as an engineer or led work involving infrastructure, platforms, APIs, data systems, or distributed systems.
You have worked with model evaluations, data-quality systems, LLMs, or other parts of building AI products.
You have helped several teams start using the same internal platform, SDK, API, or workflow.
You have worked on enterprise software where launches involved Legal, Security, Compliance, customers, or outside partners.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you will understand how work moves through the company, show us where it gets stuck, start a useful rhythm for projects and launch reviews, and automate at least one task that everyone hated doing by hand.

Within a year, leaders can see what is likely to ship and where help is needed. Teams find risks and dependencies earlier, launches no longer surprise Marketing, Legal, or Sales, and the systems you built are widely used because they make work easier and help us ship faster.

A Note On Pace

We’re building something new in a once-in-a-generation shift in technology and the legal industry, so we move at a relentless pace. We expect urgency, ownership, and good judgment even when things aren’t perfectly clear. If you need structure and consensus to do your best work, this isn’t the right place for you. If you thrive in ambiguity and growth, work with intensity, and want real responsibility, keep reading. We’re excited to meet you.

How We Work Together

GC AI is a distributed company with team members across North America, and soon Europe. We believe that because our business is AI, human connection matters more, not less. We invest in bringing people together through our hub model: regular coworking sessions, customer dinners, team and company offsites. If you’re in a location without an office, expect up to 10% travel (and more for customer-facing roles).

Team members in the San Francisco Bay Area and Provo, UT (within 50 miles of the office) work together on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. As we grow, we plan to establish permanent offices in more hub cities, and we will look to our team members to help build that in-person culture. We currently hire across the United States and Canada.

Equal Opportunity Employment

GC AI is an equal opportunity employer that supports workplace diversity and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity/expression, national origin, age, military service eligibility, veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, physical or mental disability, or any other protected class. GC AI Will Never

Stafingo is hiring an experienced IT Project Manager for a professional public-sector client in Canada.
This is an exciting opportunity for a senior project management professional to lead complex, high-impact capital IT initiatives from initiation through implementation, operational startup, and closeout.

The successful candidate will be responsible for providing end-to-end project leadership, governance, scheduling, budget oversight, risk and issue management, stakeholder engagement, vendor coordination, implementation support, and transition planning. The role will involve coordinating closely related technology initiatives and ensuring that activities, dependencies, stakeholders, timelines, and operational outcomes remain aligned throughout the project lifecycle.

Position Details

Job Title:
IT Project Manager – Capital IT Projects
Employment Type:
Contract
Location:
Remote within Canada
Start Date:
October 1st, 2026
End Date:
March 31st, 2027
Extension:
Option to extend for an additional 12 months
Working Hours:
Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM
Pay Range:
$80/hr T4 – $100/hr Incorporated
Background Check:
Basic Background Check
Submission Requirements:
Resume and responses to the Proposed Approach / Understanding of Work questions

About the Role :

The IT Project Manager will lead complex capital technology projects involving significant data migration, enterprise technology implementation, multiple stakeholder groups, and operational transition.

The successful candidate will establish project governance, define objectives and deliverables, develop and maintain detailed project schedules, manage dependencies and critical paths, monitor budgets and resources, and ensure projects remain aligned with approved scope, cost, schedule, and performance expectations.
This position requires an experienced leader who can work effectively with technical teams, business stakeholders, vendors, project sponsors, and other project managers. The ideal candidate will be comfortable managing competing priorities, resolving complex issues, communicating project status to leadership, and adapting project plans when requirements or circumstances change.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Governance :

Lead projects through initiation, planning, development, implementation, operational startup, transition, and closeout.
Define project objectives, scope, deliverables, milestones, governance structures, and success criteria.
Establish project team composition, roles, responsibilities, reporting structures, and terms of reference.
Ensure appropriate resources are available to support project delivery.
Establish and maintain project governance and project management practices.
Ensure project activities remain within approved time, cost, scope, and performance parameters.
Coordinate multiple interconnected initiatives and ensure alignment across project streams.

Planning & Scheduling

Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans and schedules.
Develop and maintain Work Breakdown Structures (WBS).
Identify project dependencies, milestones, constraints, and critical path activities.
Conduct critical path analysis and identify potential schedule impacts.
Coordinate schedules across internal teams, external stakeholders, vendors, and project partners.
Monitor progress against approved schedules and implement corrective actions where required.
Develop appropriate project charts, tables, diagrams, and other planning materials to support project analysis and decision-making.

Budget & Resource Management

Support and monitor project budget requirements.
Identify resource requirements and coordinate resource availability.
Track project expenditures and resource utilization against approved plans.
Escalate budget, resource, and capacity concerns appropriately.
Ensure project resources are aligned with approved priorities and delivery milestones.

Risk, Issue & Change Management

Identify, assess, document, and monitor project risks and issues.
Develop mitigation and contingency strategies for significant project risks.
Analyze complex project problems and formulate practical solutions.
Establish processes for managing project changes and change requests.
Assess the impact of proposed changes on scope, schedule, budget, resources, dependencies, and deliverables.
Escalate significant risks, issues, and decisions to appropriate governance bodies.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Location: Remote or On-Site in Boulder, CO
(Foresight Dx business unit, a Natera company)

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer.

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us.

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

About The Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager to lead complex diagnostic and medical device product development programs from early development through clinical trial launch, regulatory submission, and product lifecycle activities.

This individual will serve as a senior cross-functional leader, bringing the program leadership, technical understanding, and judgment needed to move complex product development programs forward in a highly regulated environment. They will lead core teams across R&D, Software, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Operations, helping teams make decisions, resolve issues, manage risk, and stay focused on delivering key milestones.

This is a hands-on role. In addition to leading programs, the Senior Program Manager will work directly with development teams on key deliverables, including Design and Development Plans (DDPs), design reviews, DHF documentation, change orders, and regulatory submission activities. Programs may span new product development, mature products, research programs, and clinical trial assay activities.

The role will also support IDE, IVDR, and 510(k) activities and drive program readiness through First Patient In (FPI). For CDx programs, this individual will partner with the CDx development and biopharma partnership teams to support the clinical trial assay and IDE/IVDR aspects of the program and ensure alignment between the clinical trial assay and CDx strategy.

What You Will Do

Lead complex, cross-functional product development programs and serve as the program leader for core teams across R&D, Software, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Operations.
Drive programs through key development milestones, design reviews, phase exits, clinical trial launch, FPI, and regulatory submission.
Translate product goals and regulatory requirements into clear plans, priorities, and decisions that enable teams to execute.
Bring cross-functional teams together to resolve technical, operational, and organizational issues and keep programs moving forward.
Identify and manage program risks, dependencies, and trade-offs, escalating issues and driving decisions through a formal portfolio governance process when needed. Communicate program progress, risks, decisions, and recommendations to functional and senior leadership.
Partner with development teams to ensure product requirements, design controls, risk management, verification/validation, and documentation are appropriately planned and executed.
Author and review key product development deliverables, including DDPs, DHF documentation, design review materials, change orders, and other development documentation.
Support preparation and execution of IDE, IVDR, 510(k), and other regulatory submissions by coordinating cross-functional deliverables and submission readiness.
For CDx programs, partner with CDx development and biopharma partnership teams to align clinical trial assay activities with the broader CDx strategy.
Apply strong knowledge of ISO 13485, IEC 62304, design controls, and regulated product development to identify gaps, anticipate risks, and help teams make sound decisions.

What You Will Bring

5-7+ years of experience in program management, product development, or a relevant combination of program leadership and functional experience in diagnostics, medical devices, biotechnology, clinical laboratories, or life sciences.
Significant experience leading complex, cross-functional product development programs in a regulated environment.
Deep practical understanding of ISO 13485, IEC 62304, design controls, and medical device/IVD development processes.
Experience leading teams through design reviews, phase exits, development milestones, and regulatory readiness activities.
Hands-on experience with product development documentation, including DDPs, DHF documentation, change orders, requirements, risk documentation, and design review materials.
Experience supporting regulatory submissions such as IDE, IVDR, 510(k), PMA, or equivalent.
Experience supporting clinical trial execution and readiness through FPI preferred.
Experience with assay, software, and systems development; NGS diagnostics and/or MRD experience strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, challenge assumptions, drive decisions, and resolve issues across functional boundaries.
Strong judgment, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment.
A hands-on, execution-oriented mindset and willingness to personally contribute to critical program and product development deliverables.
PMP certification or equivalent preferred.

Compensation & Total Rewards

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
401(k) with company match
Generous paid time off and company holidays
Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range

$$119,000.00 - $148,700.00

new_jobs.title: Marketing Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About AZX

Our mission is to accelerate positive impact in critical industries through AI transformation.

We’re growing quickly and already work with category-leaders in real estate (CBRE), energy (LevelTen Energy), logistics (Flexe), and utilities (Puget Sound Energy).

AZX is a public benefit corporation founded in 2024. We were profitable through bootstrapped consulting for the first year. In early 2026, we raised $6M to scale our operations and technology.

We work on challenges in clean energy, decarbonization, climate risk, energy systems, and global economics. We’re building our company for long-term success and aim to create the ultimate place to work for those passionate about AI and making a positive impact.

About The Role

As a Marketing Program Manager, you will own the operational machinery and discipline behind every program and campaign we run — the calendar, ABM, funnel, community, and brand — including the handoffs, the performance measurement, and the accountability that keeps them moving. It sits at the intersection of marketing, product, solutions delivery, and sales, and is the person who makes sure all prioritized campaigns, programs, and processes are executing to plan. Asana is the system of record for this work: the expectation is that anyone in the company can open it and know exactly what is running, who owns it, how it’s performing, and what’s at risk.

What You Will Do

Master the operating calendar for all GTM programs, including dependencies across product milestones, deployment timelines, and sales priorities.
Day-to-day execution support of demand generation programs targeting a narrow, high-value universe of accounts.
Content syndication and paid programs: vendor management, lead delivery and routing, list quality, and an honest assessment of what is producing qualified conversations versus noise.
AI search visibility work (AEO/GEO): maintaining the recurring audit and monitoring cadence, and tracking brand citation and mention coverage across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews.
Programs built around proof of work — case studies, deployment outcomes, and technical content developed in coordination with solutions delivery and the engineers doing the work.
Community and social management across LinkedIn, Reddit, and practitioner forums, where our audience is technical and allergic to marketing language.
Campaign infrastructure and data hygiene in the CRM: campaign objects, UTMs, lead sources, lifecycle stages, and attribution that leadership can trust.
Funnel and pipeline coordination across sales, marketing, and customer teams: routing, follow-up discipline, feedback loops on lead quality, and visibility into how programs convert into real opportunities.
Lightweight, durable processes for intake, prioritization, approvals, and retrospectives, so that program volume can grow without proportional headcount.

Core Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; MBA is a plus
2+ year’s of demonstrated ability to manage many concurrent projects/programs across stakeholders who do not report to you — this is the single most important qualification.
Demand generation and funnel management experience, with a clear understanding of pipeline mechanics beyond top-of-funnel volume.
Hands-on CRM experience (HubSpot preferred; Salesforce or equivalent acceptable).
Working fluency with the modern GTM stack — marketing automation, ad platforms, and adjacent tooling.
Strong command of Asana or comparable work management tooling, including the ability to design structures that other people will maintain.
Comfort operating with ambiguity and incomplete information, and the judgment to escalate rather than let something quietly slip.
Experience marketing complex, solution-oriented platforms into enterprise or institutional buyers with long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles is a plus
Background in enterprise SaaS, management consulting, or complex professional services is a plus
Direct experience in mission-critical industries — utilities, energy, municipal and public sector, real estate, supply chain, manufacturing, transportation, or defense.

Values And Culture Qualifications

Mission aligned—you care about climate, energy, and using technology to solve hard problems. This isn’t just a job.
Action in ambiguity—you figure out what to do when nobody tells you, and you take ownership of the outcome.
Intellectual humility—you’d rather find the right answer than be right.
Kind candor—you care about your teammates and speak honestly, without creating unnecessary conflict.
Highly productive—you have a track record of getting a lot done.

Other Qualifications (Not Required, But a Huge Plus)

Experience in B2B marketing, community management, or event coordination
Familiarity with the energy, utilities, climate, or cleantech space
Experience at an early-stage startup or building something from scratch
Existing network in energy, climate, or AI communities
Experience with marketing tools (HubSpot, Mailchimp, social scheduling platforms, etc.)

Compensation & Benefits

Salary range: $70,000–$95,000 (based on capabilities, experience, and location)
Bonus eligibility
Equity
Health insurance with meaningful coverage for dependents
Flexible paid time off
Training and learning opportunities
Fully remote team
Be part of a fast-growing, mission-driven company with industry-leading clients tackling the massive opportunity of AI transformation in critical industries

Logistics

Remote, U.S.-based. Seattle, San Francisco, New York, and Boston preferred given event and travel requirements.
We are currently unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas.
Heavy travel required for client meetings, AZX company events, and industry conferences. This role is on the ground at events regularly.

If this job sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. If you feel aligned to the company but don’t check every box, please apply anyway—we’d still love to meet you.

new_jobs.description:
About Us

RB Global (NYSE: RBA)

RB Global (NYSE: RBA) (TSX: RBA) is a leading, omnichannel marketplace that provides value-added insights, services and transaction solutions for buyers and sellers of commercial assets and vehicles worldwide. Through its auction sites in 13 countries and digital platform, RB Global serves customers in more than 170 countries across a variety of asset classes, including automotive, commercial transportation, construction, government surplus, lifting and material handling, energy, mining and agriculture.

The company’s marketplace brands include Ritchie Bros., the world’s largest auctioneer of commercial assets and vehicles offering online bidding, and IAA, a leading global digital marketplace connecting vehicle buyers and sellers. RB Global’s portfolio of brands also includes Rouse Services, which provides a complete end-to-end asset management, data-driven intelligence and performance benchmarking system; SmartEquip, an innovative technology platform that supports customers’ management of the equipment lifecycle and integrates parts procurement with both OEMs and dealers; Xcira, a leader in live simulcast auction technologies; and Veritread, an online marketplace for heavy haul transport.

RB Global full-time employees are offered medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurances. Employees are able to enroll in our company’s 401k plan and RB Global will match 100% for the first 4% contributed. Employees will also receive 15 days of PTO each year.

Job Description

The Strategic Operations Program Manager leads the end-to-end execution of strategic account programs across equipment assets lifecycle, including inspection, transportation, refurbishment, redeployment, and resale channels for North America. This role serves as the operational program owner, partnering across Sales, Operations, Logistics, Vendors and Analytics to translate customer and contractual requirements into scalable execution plans. The Program Manager ensures consistent delivery, optimizes asset flow and recovery outcomes, and drives performance through data-driven insights and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities

Primary Accountabilities

Program Execution & Asset Lifecycle Management
Own the operational execution of assigned Strategic Account programs from intake through completion across the service lifecycle
Translate contractual and strategic account requirements into clear operational workflows, task sequencing, and service milestones
Coordinate cross-functional execution across inspection, yard operations, logistics, refurbishment and resale.
Identify and proactively mitigate risks impacting asset flow, service delivery or financial outcomes
Monitor asset progression to ensure cycle time, service quality, and recovery value targets are met
Serve as the primary operational partner for assigned Strategic Accounts across Finance, Construction, OEM, Rental, Insurance, and Manufacturer Consignment segments
Act as the primary operational liaison between Sales, Site Operations, Inspection Operations, Enablement teams, and third-party vendors
Ensure alignment between customer commitments and operational execution across multiple sites and service providers
Support the rollout of customized service offerings such as a dedicated asset program, redeployment strategies, or non-auction solutions
Partner with account and operations stakeholders to resolve escalations impacting service quality, timelines, or customer satisfaction.
Program Governance, Coordination & Communication
Maintain and manage program governance artifacts including workstream trackers, action registers, service requirement documentation, and status logs
Support the development and delivery of program updates, executive summaries, and Monthly Business Review (MBR) materials
Facilitate regular status updates and business reviews with internal stakeholders and customers.
Document and support standardization of processes across sites to improve consistency and scalability.
Ensure clear and consistent communication of priorities, risks, and performance across distributed teams and locations.
Reporting Analytics & Asset Performance
Compile, validate, and maintain operational data across internal systems (e.g., MARS, Oracle, Mercury, Sales Contract Reports, + more) to support program monitoring
Develop and maintain recurring reports and dashboards using Excel, Power BI, Looker, or similar tools
Track and report on KPIs such as asset cycle time, time-to-sale, recovery value, service turnaround, and vendor performance.
Identify and analyze trends across categories, geographies, and service lines
Identify bottlenecks and recommend actions to improve throughput and financial outcomes
Provide insights and reporting to support customer reviews and internal decision-making.
Continuous Improvement & Operational Optimization
Identify operational inefficiencies and recurring execution issues across strategic programs
Partner with operations and enablement teams to implement scalable improvements
Contribute to the evolution of strategic programs and service offerings
Support change management across field operations, vendors, and internal teams

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience:

Education Required

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience
3+ years of experience in program management, operations, or asset lifecycle environments
Experience in multi-site operations, heavy equipment, logistics or industrial services preferred

Technical/Professional Accreditation

Intermediate to advanced Excel
Experience with Power BI or comparable BI tools
Familiarity with ERP, asset management, logistics or inventory systems such as MARS, Enrich, Oracle, Mercury, PO/Cost preferred

Required Experience (Type/Amount)

Strong program and/or operational management skills with high attention to detail
Ability to coordinate across distributed teams (yards, vendors, logistics)
Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority
Strong communication skills across sites, corporate and customer audiences
Analytical mindset with ability to translate data into actionable insights
Ability to manage high-volume, fast-moving operational workflows

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

This role operates in a hybrid environment, including both office and field settings such as equipment yards, inspection sites, and customer or vendor locations
Travel may be required (approximately 10–25%) depending on program needs, site locations, and customer engagements
Regular interaction with active operational environments, including equipment yards with moving machinery, varying terrain, and outdoor conditions
Physical Requirements
Ability to safely navigate outdoor industrial environments, including walking on uneven or unpaved surfaces (e.g., gravel, dirt, mud)
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods during site visits or operational reviews
May occasionally need to climb steps or ladders to access equipment for inspection or review purposes
Capability to work in varying weather conditions (heat, cold, wind, rain) when on-site
Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as safety boots, high-visibility vests, hard hats, and safety glasses
Ability to occasionally lift or move items up to 25 pounds, if necessary for site assessments or operational support

new_jobs.description:
Description

The Transformation Program Manager
is responsible for leading the end-to-end delivery of large-scale, cross-functional Global Business Services Transformation. This role serves as the central point of accountability for program execution, ensuring alignment between strategy, scope, resources, timelines, risk management, financial performance, and value realization in conjunction with a consulting partner.

The successful candidate is an experienced transformation leader who excels in navigating ambiguity, partnering with senior leaders, and orchestrating complex programs across multiple workstreams in multiple regions. They bring a balanced combination of strategic thinking, operational discipline, financial acumen, stakeholder management, and change leadership to deliver sustainable business results.

Responsibilities

Enterprise Program Leadership

Lead complex, multi-year transformation programs consisting of multiple interconnected projects and workstreams in different geographies, with internal and external partners
Translate strategic objectives into executable roadmaps, milestones, deliverables, and measurable outcomes.
Maintain accountability for program scope, schedule, budget, dependencies, risks, and benefits realization.
Drive cross-functional alignment to ensure successful achievement of transformation objectives.
Manage competing priorities and make data-driven decisions to optimize program outcomes.

Governance & Executive Engagement

Establish and lead program governance structures, decision-making forums, and executive steering committees.
Prepare executive-level reporting, dashboards, business updates, and recommendations.
Facilitate issue resolution and decision-making across senior leadership teams.
Ensure transparency of program performance through consistent reporting of milestones, risks, financials, and key performance indicators.
Escalate critical issues proactively while presenting actionable mitigation strategies.

Strategic Planning & Execution

Develop integrated program plans that align business objectives, operational requirements, technology initiatives, and organizational readiness activities.
Coordinate delivery across multiple teams, functions, and external partners.
Monitor progress against key milestones and implement corrective actions when required.
Drive continuous improvement of program management processes, tools, and methodologies.
Ensure effective dependency management across initiatives and business functions.

Risk, Financial & Value Management

Establish and maintain comprehensive risk management frameworks.
Identify, assess, and mitigate program risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies.
Manage program budgets, forecasts, resource plans, and financial performance.
Track and validate business outcomes, value realization, and return on investment.
Partner with Finance and business leaders to ensure financial commitments and benefits are achieved.

Stakeholder & Change Leadership

Build strong relationships across executive leaders, functional leaders, and project teams.
Drive alignment among diverse stakeholder groups with competing priorities.
Collaborate closely with Change Enablement, Communications, and Business Readiness teams to support adoption and sustainment.
Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Lead through influence while effectively navigating organizational complexity and resistance.

Qualifications

Experience:

10+ years leading complex enterprise programs, strategic initiatives, or large-scale transformations.
Experience working with executive leadership teams and steering committees.
Experience leading cross-functional teams in matrixed environments.
Proven track record delivering programs involving process, organizational, operational, and technology change.
Experience managing multimillion-dollar budgets and value realization initiatives.
PMP, PgMP, Prosci, Lean Six Sigma, Agile, or related certifications considered an asset

Skills:

Proven ability to lead large-scale, complex, cross-functional transformation programs from strategy through execution.
Strong program and portfolio management expertise, including planning, governance, resource management, dependency management, and delivery oversight.
Experience partnering with external consulting firms
Exceptional executive communication skills with the ability to influence, align, and build credibility across all organizational levels.
Demonstrated experience establishing governance frameworks and facilitating executive decision-making and issue resolution.
Strong financial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and value realization tracking.
Advanced risk management and problem-solving skills, with the ability to proactively identify, assess, and mitigate program risks and issues.
Ability to navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities, and make sound decisions in fast-paced, evolving environments.
Strategic and enterprise mindset with the ability to connect business objectives, operational priorities, and measurable outcomes.

new_jobs.title: AI Content Program Manager, Chatbot
new_jobs.description:
HoneyBook is the leading AI-powered business management platform for service-based business owners. Designed to enhance - not replace - independent professionals. HoneyBook’s AI-powered tools help businesses attract leads, connect with clients, book projects, and manage payments more efficiently. With AI seamlessly integrated into every workflow, entrepreneurs can focus on their craft while scaling their businesses with confidence. Since its founding in 2013, HoneyBook has powered over 25 million client relationships and processed more than $12 billion in transactions, helping independent businesses grow faster and smarter.

Our culture is built on five core values that inform everything we do. We encourage collaboration, feedback, ownership, and maintain a growth mindset. We know experience comes in many forms - some visible on your resume, others not. No one candidate will be a 100% perfect match to our description, so if you thrive in a fast-paced, intellectually curious environment and have relevant experience, we encourage you to apply.

About The Role

As an AI Content Program Manager
, you'll sit within the Knowledge & Instructional Content team (KIC) that supports both our members (customers) and our Support Specialists. You'll own the strategy and execution of our support chatbot, the front line for how members get fast, accurate answers, and you'll support the full lifecycle of the Help Center articles and internal Support documentation that feed it.

You'll set the direction for how our chatbot resolves member issues, from what it should be able to handle to how content gets structured so it can act on it, and you'll build the Help Center content and Support documentation that equip Support Specialists with clear, dependable guidance across every channel. From building new content to optimizing existing workflows, your work will directly influence the clarity, consistency, and effectiveness of our member and agent experiences. Every article you publish, update, or structure directly determines how members get fast, accurate answers. AI resolution is one of the most important levers the team owns, and you're accountable for moving it. As chatbot resolution matures, you'll set the strategy for how we prioritize and structure content investment across the AI resolution funnel.

Here are a few of the things you will do

AI Resolution Strategy: Own the analysis of chatbot resolution data in partnership with Member Care and AI Operations, identify where content gaps are limiting AI resolution rates, drive the roadmap for what gets built, updated, or restructured next, and help evaluate whether a single-platform or multi-platform chatbot strategy best serves our members.
Chatbot Build & Configuration: Work directly in our chatbot platform (currently Intercom) to configure and maintain our support chatbot, and use Claude Code to build and maintain the data connectors that power it.
AI Process Innovation: Go beyond using LLMs for drafting, content gap analysis, and basic data synthesis. Identify where AI can change how the team works, and own the evaluation and rollout of new AI tools and workflows.
App Development: Build functional internal tools using no-code/low-code platforms (such as Lovable) to solve real team friction points. You'll ship internal tools frequently, with support and context from the team.
AI-Driven Content Strategy: Utilize Large Language Models (LLMs) for drafting, brainstorming, and basic data synthesis to accelerate content production.
Member-Facing Support: Support the creation, maintenance, and ongoing improvement of member-facing Help Center content that supports fast, accurate self-serve resolution.
Technical Documentation: Write clear, actionable technical how-tos and process documentation that guide members and Support Specialists to the most efficient and effective resolution.
Internal Governance: Help maintain internal Support documentation so it is clear, accurate, and structured for both human and AI-assisted resolution. In practice, this means writing procedures our Support bot can act on, documenting decision logic for connector builds, and incorporating QA findings into content revisions, as well as human-readable accuracy. The quality of this documentation is a direct input to how effectively AI resolves member issues at scale.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Own the working relationship with Member Care, Product, QA, Marketing, and cross-functional partners to anticipate content needs, set priorities, and ensure documentation reflects current product behavior.

Here Is What We're Looking For In a Candidate

AI Expertise: You go beyond using AI tools like Gemini and Claude to draft and brainstorm. You understand how chatbot content architecture affects resolution rates, and you can bring informed opinions to conversations about AI strategy, not just execute against it. You can learn new tools quickly and are curious about how technology can make your content, and the systems it feeds, more effective.
Technical Fluency: You have hands-on experience working in chatbot platforms such as Intercom (our current platform). You'll use Claude Code daily to build and maintain data connectors, so prior experience with it is ideal, though comparable experience with similar technical tools works too. You're comfortable owning the technical side of chatbot configuration, not just the content that feeds it.
Strong Communication: You possess strong writing skills and can take a complex product and make it easy to understand through structured, action-oriented documentation.
Data-Driven Mindset: You have an understanding of how analytics impact strategic decisions and guide content prioritization and search optimization. You are comfortable reviewing chatbot resolution data or Help Center analytics to identify gaps and prioritize what to write or update next.
Systems Thinking: You have a strong grasp of systems thinking and independently connect documentation to Support workflows and Member Care operations, spotting cross-team dependencies before they become blockers.
Efficiency & Growth: You love finding opportunities to improve existing content and can independently move projects forward while balancing multiple priorities.

The good stuff:

Mission-driven:
You'll be joining more than just another startup. Our members’ success is at the heart of everything we do.

Impact:
We move quickly and encourage every employee to push the envelope. Our best ideas come from out-of-the-box thinking and innovation; be ready to fail fast and often!

Compensation:
We offer a competitive salary and meaningful equity grants.

Benefits & perks:
From wellness programs to exceptional family leave policies, the health and happiness of our employees are foremost.

Our core values:

People come first:
We prioritize people as we explore opportunities and work through challenges.

Raise the bar:
We push for greatness—for ourselves, each other, and our members.

Own it:
Trust and ownership let us make decisions with confidence.

We love what we do:
We bring passion to our work and love what we create for our members.

Keep it real:
Authenticity, respect, and transparency are at our core.

The opportunity at HoneyBook is huge. Our primary customers today are creative businesses that generate $150M in revenue per year in the US. Founded in 2013, HoneyBook is based in San Francisco and Tel Aviv, has raised $498M, and is funded by Tiger Global Management, Norwest Venture Partners, Aleph, Hillsven Capital, OurCrowd, Durable Capital Partners LP, Vintage Investment Partners, Battery Ventures, Citi Ventures, Zeev Ventures, and 01 Advisors.

Title: Program Manager

About Us:

The company is a leader in RF/antenna measurement innovation, transforming aerospace, defense, satellite, and wireless industries.
Job Summary:

The Program Manager is a key member of the customer support team and will oversee the delivery of new systems, parts and upgrades for domestic and international customers. new_jobs.description:

At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them.

AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward.

The Role

AMD’s Data Center Platform Engineering Group (DPEG) designs, builds, and delivers industry‑leading technology platforms that power the world’s most advanced cloud, AI, and telecom infrastructures. We develop cloud‑enabling server platforms and system solutions that allow the world’s leading companies to transform ideas into reality at global scale. Our customers are forward‑looking, and so are we continuously innovating to stay ahead of the next technological challenge.

As part of the Data Center Platform Engineering organization, the Staff Product Development Technical Program Manager will lead the management and execution of AI server and hyperscale server platform programs with significant customer and business impact. This role is responsible for driving system‑level hardware execution across the full product lifecycle, from early product definition and architecture through design, validation, production release, ramp, and end‑of‑life.

The ideal candidate will operate as a system‑level leader and integrator, coordinating complex, cross‑functional teams to deliver high‑quality, manufacturable, and scalable server platforms that meet aggressive schedule, cost, and quality targets.

The Person

You are a hardware‑focused Technical Program Manager with strong system‑level instincts and the ability to lead highly complex programs that span electrical, mechanical, power, thermal, manufacturing, and supply chain domains.

You work closely with System Architecture, Engineering, Reliability, Compliance, and Business and Account Teams to translate platform requirements and product specifications into clear, executable hardware programs with well‑defined milestones, risks, and deliverables.
You lead cross‑functional hardware execution teams to plan, develop, validate, and launch server platforms on schedule, ensuring alignment across engineering, firmware/BIOS, manufacturing, quality, operations, and supplier organizations.
You excel at driving clarity in ambiguous environments, defining program structure, execution plans, and decision frameworks that enable teams to move quickly while managing technical and operational risk.
You are comfortable operating at multiple levels from detailed hardware execution reviews to executive‑level program discussions and can clearly articulate tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
You bring a strong ownership mindset, proactively identifying issues, driving resolution across organizations, and holding teams accountable for delivery without relying on formal authority.
You naturally mentor and influence others, helping raise the bar for program rigor, system‑level thinking, and execution excellence across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Own system‑level technical program strategy and execution across feature delivery, product quality, and continuity of supply, balancing technical trade‑offs, customer requirements, and business priorities across the full product lifecycle.
Drive cross‑functional alignment between Engineering, Product Management, Sales, Operations, and Supply Chain, translating platform capabilities, system constraints, and roadmap strategy into executable plans that support customer commitments and business outcomes.
Lead execution of highly complex, multi‑disciplinary system solutions, spanning Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBAs), mechanical architecture, power and thermals, operating systems, BMC, BIOS, solution software, diagnostics, validation, and test while coordinating internal teams and external vendors to meet cost, quality, and schedule objectives.
Act as a system‑level integrator, ensuring alignment across hardware, firmware, and software architectures, proactively managing inter‑team dependencies and surfacing systemic risks early.
Ensure designs meet manufacturability, reliability, serviceability, and scalability requirements, partnering closely with manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams to enable production readiness and long‑term lifecycle sustainability.
Establish and lead core execution mechanisms, including weekly program reviews and milestone checkpoints with global, cross‑functional stakeholders, driving accountability, resolving escalations, and ensuring on‑time milestone delivery.
Identify, assess, and communicate program risks at the system level, defining mitigation plans and driving cross‑functional hardware and software solutions to minimize impact to schedule, cost, quality, and supply continuity.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing clear, data‑driven program status, decision trade‑offs, and escalation paths for high‑impact system and execution issues.
Own program governance, documentation, and communications throughout the development lifecycle, ensuring timely, accurate dissemination of decisions, execution status, and deliverables to internal stakeholders, customers, and partners.
Define, track, and publish program metrics and KPIs, using quantitative insights to support execution reviews, continuous improvement, and program health reporting.
Lead Bill of Materials (BOM) strategy and execution from early prototype through production, facilitating BOM reviews to ensure technical integrity, cost optimization, supplier readiness, and alignment with manufacturing and sourcing strategies.
Partner with engineering and configuration management teams to manage BOM lifecycle transitions, ensuring disciplined change control, traceability, and alignment from preliminary design through high‑volume manufacturing.
Mentor and influence other Technical Program Managers and technical leads, elevating execution rigor, system‑level thinking, and operational excellence across the organization.

Preferred Experience

Proven experience owning system‑level hardware programs across the full development lifecycle, from architecture definition and early prototyping through production ramp and sustaining.
Strong technical depth in hardware systems, including experience with one or more of the following:
Demonstrated ability to manage cross‑functional execution across hardware engineering, BMC/BIOS, manufacturing, quality, operations, and supply chain teams.
Experience driving design for manufacturability, reliability, and serviceability, working closely with manufacturing engineers, suppliers, and contract manufacturers.
Hands‑on experience managing Bill of Materials (BOM) lifecycle, including prototype, pre‑production, and production stages, with disciplined change control and configuration management.
Strong program leadership and communication skills, with a track record of driving alignment, resolving escalations, and influencing without formal authority across multiple organizations.
Data‑driven decision‑making capability, including defining and tracking hardware execution metrics, risk burndown, and program health indicators
Customer-facing experience, supporting launch readiness, field quality investigations, or hardware execution discussions with strategic customers or partners.

Academic Credentials

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Advanced degree (MS) in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field is preferred.
Formal project management education, PMP / Scrum Master

Interested in working on cutting-edge blockchain technology and creating equitable access to the global financial system? Since 2014, the mission-driven team at the Stellar Development Foundation (SDF) has helped fuel the tremendous growth of the Stellar blockchain network, an open-source platform that operates at high-scale today. Developers and companies around the world build on it, and the SDF team is expanding to support the rapidly growing and changing Stellar ecosystem.

The Stellar Development Foundation (SDF) is looking for a talented and experienced Senior Program Manager, Partner Programs
to help key partners integrate with the Stellar Network. In this role, you will coordinate across our partners and internal stakeholders (Engineering, BD, Marketing, Product, Account Management) to build innovative blockchain solutions. SDF's partners span the globe and include some of the most innovative software and financial companies in the world.

In This Role, You Will

Manage, plan, and direct software and product development activities from launch to completion, with overall responsibility for delivering on time and at high quality.
Own long-term partner integration roadmaps and the success of multiple partners in the Stellar ecosystem.
Host and drive partner meetings with technical and business stakeholders.
Identify and manage technical dependencies and blockers across partner and internal engineering teams.
Maintain partner-related documentation, including milestone plans, dependencies, schedules, risks, and meeting notes.
Measure program performance, analyzing the successful completion of short- and long-term goals against company and team OKRs.
Define process frameworks, program plan templates, tools, and best practices that can be adopted throughout the organization.

You Have

7+ years of experience managing software development programs in the financial services industry, some of which took place in a blockchain startup or small-company environment.
Comfort engaging in technical discussions — APIs, integration flows, system dependencies — enough to coordinate credibly with engineering, track technical risks and blockers, and translate fluidly between technical and business stakeholders. You don't need to write the code, but you need to understand what's being built well enough to drive it.
Familiarity with blockchain/crypto concepts, or a demonstrated ability to ramp quickly on a complex, unfamiliar technical domain.
A habit of using AI tools to work smarter — you look for ways to apply AI to your day-to-day, whether that's drafting and summarizing documentation, accelerating research, streamlining reporting, or automating repetitive workflows, and you're eager to help the team do the same.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent leadership skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with partners from various backgrounds and positions.
Great organizational skills, including attention to detail, multitasking, and creating and instituting processes to streamline workflows.
Experience with program and project management tools like Jira, Airtable, Asana, Confluence, and Google Suite.
An independent nature and results-driven attitude — you're good at identifying priorities and working in an environment with dynamic objectives.
A knack for problem-solving — you have an eye for untold problems in the program life cycle and create solutions to minimize or mitigate them.

Enthusiasm for working in a startup environment with some level of ambiguity and wearing multiple hats.

You have a deeper curiosity about new blockchain technologies (for example, DeFi, Earn, contract tokens) and cryptocurrencies.
You have worked directly with external partners in the capacity of program manager, project manager, delivery manager, technical program manager or consultant.

Competitive health, dental & vision coverage with most plans covered at 100% for the employee + any dependents

Stellar is more than a blockchain. Powered by a decentralized, fast, scalable, and uniquely sustainable network made for financial products and services and a thriving and passionate ecosystem that includes a non-profit organization driven by a mission, Stellar is paving the path to unlock the world’s economic potential through blockchain technology. Who We Are

Born digital, UST transforms lives through the power of technology. We walk alongside our clients and partners, embedding innovation and agility into everything they do. We help them create transformative experiences and human-centered solutions for a better world.

UST is a mission-driven group of 29,000+ practical problem solvers and creative thinkers in more than 30 countries. Our entrepreneurial teams are empowered to innovate, act nimbly, and create a lasting and sustainable impact for our clients, their customers, and the communities in which we live.

With us, you’ll create a boundless impact that transforms your career—and the lives of people across the world.

Visit us at UST.com.

You Are

UST is searching for an experienced Technical Program Manager to lead complex enterprise transformation, implementation, and migration programs.

The Opportunity

Lead and oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of large-scale transformation programs, including design, build, testing, and deployment activities.
Manage complex implementation and migration projects, ensuring delivery within agreed scope, timeline, budget, and quality parameters.
Develop and maintain integrated project plans, accounting for dependencies, constraints, resource availability, and organizational priorities.
Drive technical program governance, ensuring alignment across multiple applications, workstreams, and stakeholder groups.
Facilitate collaboration among business, technology, architecture, and vendor teams to achieve program objectives.
Build consensus and proactively resolve conflicts across multiple stakeholders, teams, and organizations.

Utilize project and program management tools such as Jira and Azure DevOps (ADO) for planning, tracking, reporting, and governance.
Identify, assess, manage, and mitigate project and program risks to ensure successful delivery.

Ensure accountability across teams by enforcing responsibilities and decision-making authorities as defined in the approved RACSI/RACI framework.
Monitor program performance through KPIs, milestones, and executive reporting, providing clear status updates to senior leadership.
Drive continuous improvement in project delivery processes, governance standards, and execution methodologies.

Robust experience (12-15 Yrs) in large implementation or migration projects

Ability to develop Integrated Project plan with constraints
Ability to drive consensus and resolve conflicts across multiple parties

Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Department Overview

The Command Center Software and Services team delivers solutions and maintenance services to the public safety sector. We are committed to providing technology and tools which will allow customers to focus on their mission, and enable them to respond faster with smarter and safer decisions.

The projects contained in the Command Center portfolio include large Statewide, Regional, and major Municipal Public Safety Applications (CAD, Mobile, Records Management, Crime Analysis, and Jail), Emergency Call Handling/Next Gen 911 solutions, Asset Management Solutions, and other applications used in the Command Center.

Our foundational principle is an unwavering focus on the customer. This customer-centric approach guides every decision, strategy, and innovation, aiming to understand, meet, and exceed customer needs. We strive to be a trusted partner, invested in their long-term success. This commitment requires continuous listening, proactive problem-solving, and delivering exceptional value and service at every customer touchpoint.

Job Description

Motorola Solutions is seeking a Senior Federal Software Program Manager
to direct large-scale, enterprise software deployments and complex technology initiatives for federal government and public safety clients. In this high-visibility, remote role, you will hold end-to-end accountability for program governance, financial performance (P&L), cross-functional team leadership, federal compliance, and client satisfaction. You will act as both a trusted advisor to government stakeholders and a strategic partner to internal growth teams to shape competitive proposals and deliver mission-critical software solutions.

This is a fully remote position, with up to 50% travel to customer sites across North America. Preference for candidates based in Eastern/Central locations.

Key Responsibilities

Project Planning, Governance & Methodologies

Develops, manages, and implements the master project plan using automated project management tools, processes, and procedures.
Defines and measures the performance relating to achieving specific goals.
Utilizes best practice project management methodologies to ensure maximum project effectiveness.
Ensures designated standards and processes are followed for assigned projects.

Team Leadership & Internal Operations

Contribute to the development and refinement of internal operating procedures to support continuous improvement and corporate operational development.

new_jobs.title: Supply Chain Security Manager
new_jobs.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

THE ROLE

AMD Corporate Security is seeking a Supply Chain Security Corporate Investigator to join its global Corporate Security Investigations team. This role reports to the Director of Corporate Security Investigations and partners closely with the Supply Chain Security & Product Loss program to protect AMD’s products, facilities, and partners across a high-value, high-velocity global supply chain spanning wafer fabrication, assembly and testing, third-party logistics (3PL), and distribution.

As AMD scales its AI infrastructure and data center business, the integrity, security, and traceability of our supply chain, from silicon to system, have never mattered more. You will conduct site security audits and due diligence assessments of suppliers, manufacturing partners, and logistics providers; investigate product loss, theft, and diversion; and help ensure that high-value AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, and other AMD products are secured from the point of manufacture through authorized distribution.

You will work in a fast-paced, global environment where your investigative, analytical, and cross-functional partnership skills will play a direct role in protecting AMD’s brand, revenue, and reputation.

This newly created role supports AMD’s continued growth in high-value AI and data center products and the ongoing maturation of its global supply chain security program. The successful candidate will bring current, modern investigative practices to help strengthen and evolve how AMD protects its most valuable and sought-after AI products.

THE PERSON

Insatiable curiosity and a passion for uncovering facts and following them wherever they lead, along with sound judgment about when and how to escalate.
Ability to build trust and credibility across a global, cross-functional organization, including with external partners, suppliers, and law enforcement.
Strong analytical and reporting skills, with the ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible documentation for leadership.
Comfortable operating independently across time zones and cultures, with sensitivity to local laws, customs, and labor practices during site visits and audits.
Creative, practical problem-solver who can balance risk mitigation with business continuity.
Collaborative, can-do colleague who communicates with discretion and professionalism, especially when handling sensitive or confidential matters.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct on-site and virtual security audits and due diligence assessments of suppliers, manufacturing sites, and third-party logistics (3PL) facilities to ensure the secure handling, storage, warehousing, distribution, and reclamation of AMD products.
Investigate incidents of product theft, loss, diversion, and counterfeiting, partnering with Global Product Investigations and regional security teams across the Americas, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Greater China, as needed.
Perform open-source intelligence (OSINT) research and due diligence on new and existing supply chain partners to identify security, integrity, and reputational risks.
Support compliance with the Customs-Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (C-TPAT) and other trade security programs across AMD sites, product storage facilities, and cross-dock facilities.
Prepare clear, accurate, and well-documented investigation reports and audit findings, including recommended corrective and remediation actions, for leadership review.
Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Global Trade, Procurement, Information Security, and business unit teams to assess and mitigate third-party and supply chain risks in accordance with AMD’s Third-Party Risk Management standards.
Support the security of high-value, high-demand AI infrastructure products, including accelerators, GPUs, and CPUs, as they move through manufacturing, assembly, testing, and distribution.
Track corrective action plans following audits or incidents and follow up to confirm timely closure.
Respond to and help coordinate on-site theft, loss, and other security incidents reported through regional security channels.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of AMD’s supply chain security program, policies, and audit methodology.

Preferred Experience

Five or more years of experience in corporate investigations, supply chain security, loss prevention, or related risk or security roles.
Experience in the technology, semiconductor, or high-value manufacturing industry is a plus.
Experience with global logistics and trade security frameworks, such as C-TPAT and TAPA, is a plus.
Experience conducting supplier or third-party due diligence and site security assessments.
Willingness and ability to travel internationally to supplier, manufacturing, and logistics sites as needed.
Knowledge of state-of-the-art investigative practices, supported by recent, hands-on experience with real-world cases rather than reliance on legacy methods or outdated tools.
Strong understanding of evolving technology risks, including how digital, cyber, and physical threats intersect across a global supply chain.
Demonstrated ability to identify, assess, and respond to increasingly sophisticated threats targeting AI technology and intellectual property, including nation-state, insider, and organized theft schemes targeting high-value computing and accelerator products.

ACADEMIC AND PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS

Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Relevant certification, such as Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), Certified Protection Professional (CPP), or Professional Certified Investigator (PCI), is a plus.

LOCATION

Austin, Texas. Other AMD global sites may be considered based on business needs.

The cybersecurity analyst monitors NLR's networks and computing systems for suspicious or unwanted activity, investigates the causes and impacts of the activity, and ensures any related security issues are remediated. In-depth understanding of common cybersecurity concepts and threats and ability to apply that knowledge to strengthen the security operations function.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager, Revenue Operations
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

We are looking for a delivery-focused Project Manager to run acquisition migrations end-to-end as Beacon standardizes each newly acquired company onto a common GTM stack. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who runs several projects at once against a hard deadline, keeps a lot of moving parts coordinated, and raises the bar on the quality of work around them.

Beacon acquires roughly one software company per week which is then integrated into our standardized GTM stack. This role partners with newly acquired companies starting from the first discovery call, through CRM and Support Ticketing builds, until systems are fully rolled out. This role coordinates internal resources and ensures the portfolio company is trained on the tech stack while adhering to an SLA and making the process more repeatable with every acquisition.

This role is responsible for running the project, meaning holding the timeline, managing the stakeholders, directing the build resources, and making sure what ships is right. This role will be partnered with a technical RevOps resource to help with deeper technical support, but this role will be responsible for speaking to the toolset at a high-level.

What you would own

Migration delivery. Acquisition migrations against our SLA, owned end to end: scoping, project planning, sequencing the CRM and Support Ticketing builds, coordinating data migration, and making sure the team is trained and confident at go-live. You would lead discovery calls to assess their current stack and map it to Beacon's standards, hold the plan and the timeline across several concurrent migrations, manage dependencies and risks before they become slips, and own the status.
Contractor direction and quality. You would direct the work of pooled implementation contractors assigned to your migrations, pull in technical support when a problem genuinely needs it, make day-to-day scope and sequencing calls within the documented playbook, and escalate only genuine exceptions.
Delivery process. Improving the migration playbook as you run against it — tightening the plan, the checklists, and the handoffs so each acquisition goes faster and more predictably than the last.

Who you are

You have 3–5 years project or program management, running implementation, migration or change management projects — ideally in B2B SaaS, professional services, or consulting. You ideally have managed multiple projects concurrently against firm deadlines..
You are literate in Go-To-Market systems. You understand how a CRM and a support platform are put together and can scope a build, and hold a credible conversation with a founder about their GTM tech stack.
You have directed the work of others — contractors, an agency pod, or junior admins — even without formal people management.
A confident stakeholder-facing communicator. You’re a people person who can understand hesitant stakeholders and help them feel excited during a period of a lot of change.
Strong judgment under ambiguity. You make defensible calls from a playbook instead of escalating everything, and you know which exceptions genuinely warrant escalation.
A quality bar you set rather than inherit. You care how the build looks six months after go-live, not just at handoff.
Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time
A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan
The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you

Nice to have

Formal project management training or certification (PMP or similar).
Familiar with project management tools (Asana, JIRA, Monday.com).
Hands-on CRM experience (HubSpot, Salesforce, PipeDrive, Zoho, etc.)
Hands-on Support experience (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, etc.)
M&A exposure, particularly post-close systems consolidation.
Familiarity with migration tooling or scripting that moves data faster and more reliably than manual imports allow.

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

Our Technology Strategy and Operations team is seeking a Project Manager to lead administration of the IT Strategic Portfolio Management processes and tool. You will implement SPM capabilities and processes to be utilized across the IT department, maintaining overall responsibility for the SPM processes and coordination across multiple IT PMO teams. Configure and manage workflows within the SPM system to streamline project intake, prioritization, and approval processes.
Ensure adherence to established portfolio management methodologies and governance procedures.

2 to 4 years progressive technology experience with administrating strategic portfolio management tools at an enterprise level.
Strong understanding of project management principles and methodologies
